core_classification.analysis: Oswald directly avows that he loves Corinne “more than ever,” primarily presenting his intensified love as true in order to counter her fatalistic conclusion. The continuation “my whole soul is yours” gives slight support to relational dedication, but there is no clear new or renewed undertaking. His interruption and emotional urgency do not independently establish expressive/reflexive force.
core_classification.ambiguity: The phrase “quand toute mon âme est à toi” may weakly invoke devotion or commitment, but it is more naturally read as further description of Oswald’s present attachment.

utterance_status.description: Oswald directly addresses Corinne; the love avowal is grammatically embedded in a contrastive temporal clause (“Quand je t’aime plus que jamais”) and is left syntactically unfinished when Corinne continues speaking.

contextual_interpretation: Corinne interprets the nun’s renunciation as an omen that her own happiness is over. Oswald interrupts with an intensified avowal of love and total attachment, attempting to contradict and reassure her. The ominous setting and urgent delivery heighten the scene, but the core utterance remains principally a truth-conditional avowal rather than a reflexive discharge or explicit commitment.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “Quand je t’aime plus que jamais” (“When I love you more than ever”).
evidence.supports: Strong truth-conditional support: Oswald presents his current love for Corinne, intensified relative to the past, as true.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Oswald continues, “quand toute mon âme est à toi...” (“when my whole soul is yours...”).
evidence.supports: Reinforces the avowal of profound attachment and supplies limited pressure toward relational dedication, though not an explicit undertaking.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Oswald’s words interrupt Corinne immediately after she says that “the flowers of life” have been cast behind her forever.
evidence.supports: Shows that the avowal functions contextually as contradiction and reassurance in response to Corinne’s fatalism.

evidence.quotation_or_description: The narration says “interrompit Oswald,” while Corinne then continues her own speech.
evidence.supports: Establishes urgent interruption but provides no positive evidence that the words escape as a reflex-like expressive discharge.

evidence.quotation_or_description: The occurrence is identified as an affirmative present-tense explicit love expression in Chapter VII of Madame de Staël’s Corinne; ou, l’Italie.
evidence.supports: Confirms the occurrence’s grammatical form and bibliographic location.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T/P/E adequately represents the core force: a strong avowal with at most a weak undertone of relational dedication. The scene’s urgency, ominous symbolism, and reassuring purpose are contextual rather than missing dimensions of core force.
